title: Minimum Cover Window
statement: You are given a long text `S` and a short pattern `T`. Find the shortest contiguous substring of `S` that contains every character of `T`, counting repeats: if `T` has two `a` characters, the substring must contain at least two `a` characters.
If several shortest substrings exist, print the one that starts earliest in `S`. If no substring works, print `-1`.
inputFormat: The first line contains the string `S`.
The second line contains the string `T`.
Both are nonempty and contain only lowercase letters `a`–`z`.
outputFormat: Print the shortest covering substring, or `-1`.

examples.explanation: "banc" contains a, b and c, and no shorter window does.
"bcd" and "dab" both have length 3; "bcd" starts earlier.

starter.output: the shortest substring of S covering T (earliest on ties), or -1

private.complexity: O(|S| + |T|) two-pointer window with letter counts and a 'missing' counter.
private.notes: Record a window only when it is strictly shorter than the best so far; scanning left to right then gives the earliest start among equal lengths.
